notes:
**Windows** — run `ruze_0.0.15_x64-setup.exe`.
**Linux** — `flatpak install ruze-0.0.15.flatpak`, then `flatpak run com.ruze.chat`.
**Android** — sideload `ruze-0.0.15.apk`. arm64 devices, Android 8.0 or newer.

---

### Added

- **Add a device without ever showing your account.** Account settings has
  *Add another device*: it puts a code on screen, the new device scans or pastes
  it under *Join an account*, and both then show the same six digits. Allow it
  on the first device and the account moves across — same name, same history,
  recognised in every server you are already in.

  What is on screen is not the account. It is where to find this device plus a
  random secret good for three minutes and one use. Someone who photographs it
  can start a pairing; they cannot finish one, because finishing needs somebody
  to press Allow on the device that already holds the account — and what they
  get instead is a prompt naming a device you do not recognise.

  Both devices have to be online and running Ruze at the same time. This is a
  live connection between the two, not a code redeemed later against something
  else, and the app says so before you go and fetch the other device — including
  when this one has not reached the network yet, in which case the code can be
  scanned but never answered.

  Reading a QR code needs a camera, so scanning is offered on phones and pasting
  everywhere. The recovery phrase still works and is still there; it is now the
  fallback rather than the way.

### Fixed

- **"The installer threw" now says what threw.** The in-app Android update
  reported a Java exception by name and sent the useful half — the class and
  the message — to a log only a developer with a cable attached could read. It
  comes back with the error now.

  The likely cause of that exception is already fixed as of 0.0.14: release
  builds are minified, and the class the update goes through is reached only
  from Rust over JNI, so R8 could not see it was used and removed it. Both that
  class and the voice-call service are now kept whole rather than by naming
  their entry points — `UpdateInstaller` is a Kotlin `object`, so the method
  named in the rule is a shim that reaches the real one through an INSTANCE
  field, and every link in that chain has to survive.

  Worth knowing: an app cannot fix this for itself. The build that has the bug
  cannot deliver the build that fixes it, so 0.0.14 or later has to be
  installed by hand once.
